issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
In the last step of search near, wiredtiger walks the cursor back and forth to find a visible value. If there are a lot of invisible data to the reader, the search near performs poorly. As for each invisible key it inspects, it needs to do a history store search to check if there is a visible version in the history store or not. And most of the time, it will find nothing there.

*Scope of the ticket:*
 Brainstorm optimisations to improve the search near performance in this case and create separate tickets.

SERVER-61185 - Use prefix_search for unique index lookup
Status: Closed
Due Date: Not Set
Assignee: Louis Williams

Last Comment: Louis Williams - Over 49 months ago
This change improves the performance of inserting documents into collections with unique indexes. The change was not backported uniformly to all branches. For 4.4: We have disabled the optimized behavior by default, but it can be enabled with a setParameter "wiredTigerPrefixSearchForUniqueIndexes". This was done in an attempt to prevent making significant behavioral changes on a more stable branch. For 5.0: We have enabled the optimized behavior by default, but it can be disabled with a setParameter "wiredTigerPrefixSearchForUniqueIndexes". This may be done for users who do not want to expose themselves to this behavior on a stable branch. For all newer versions, this behavior is enabled by default and cannot be disabled.

comments.body: [~jie.chen], didn't you create a ticket related to this so we don't check the HS if not needed when calling search_near?

[~etienne.petrel] not yet, was planning to do a little extra investigation if this would really pose a problem. But now we have proof that this does actually reach poor performance.

In my test there was no history values, but when searching at a timestamp where no keys would be visible in the tree, it was still performing alot of extraneous search near calls in the history. This also cluttered the {{cursor_next_skip_ge_100}} statistics, further information about this is found in WT-8107.

I talked with this with [~haseeb.bokhari] on this, potentially thought about if it was possible for a particular btree entry (either through a flag or other means), to be able to determine if there is a need to read the HS.

[~jie.chen], if I remember correctly, we talked about setting a flag on the key that would indicate that the last HS search for this key didn't yield anything. But there are few pitfalls there such as what was the timestamp used for last search or how the snapshot looked like for the reader at that time, etc.

This python test reproduces the issue. If you increase the number of rows, the test will run slower and slower.

    uri = "table:search_near09"

        cursor = self.session.open_cursor(self.uri)
        for i in range(1, nrows + 1):

            cursor[i] = value
            self.session.commit_transaction('commit_timestamp=' + self.timestamp_str(commit_ts))
        cursor.close()
    
    # Evict the page to force reconciliation.
    def evict(self, nrows):
        evict_cursor = self.session.open_cursor(self.uri, None, "debug=(release_evict)")
        for i in range(1, nrows + 1):
            self.session.begin_transaction()
            v = evict_cursor[i]
            self.assertEqual(evict_cursor.reset(), 0)
            self.session.rollback_transaction()

            thread = Thread(target = self.search_near)
            thread.start()

[~brian.lane] I just tested prefix search with the reproducer with 40000 keys. A single search near is 10000 times faster. From 0.6 second reduced to 0.00006 second.
Thanks [~chenhao.qu] that is quite a difference!  The cpp tests mentioned in the meeting today were already in future sprints, but they are both now in the next sprint.  WT-8091 and WT-8286.
[~brian.lane] Can we bring them forward to this sprint?
[~chenhao.qu] I put them at the top of the next sprint, if you feel you have capacity feel free to bring one into the current sprint.
[~brian.lane] I think we are now in a good shape to adopt prefix search. Please inform the server team we are ready.
The rest work of this ticket is to verify the performance of unique index insertion is back to normal in mongodb after it switches to prefix search.
The work is shifted to SERVER-61185. Close this ticket.
